description: Lambda handler (lambda/handler.py) for an HTTP API (payload v2.0) that runs the full photo-to-depth path: Bedrock Nova vision (pixel-only), the reused deterministic depth engine, Open-Meteo rainfall fusion, DynamoDB persistence, best-effort SNS, plus /reports, /seed, /health and a demo mode. Independent of FEAT-002/003.
steps: Create lambda/handler.py. Read engine/depth_engine.py FIRST to confirm exact names; the handler imports from a sibling module: `from depth_engine import REFERENCE_HEIGHTS_M, DepthInput, compute_depth, fuse_rainfall` (the engine is vendored next to the handler at deploy time; do NOT import from ../engine).

Define constants: SETTLEMENTS = {'Mathare': (-1.2595, 36.8580), 'Mukuru': (-1.3167, 36.8667)}; MODEL_ID = os.environ.get('MODEL_ID','amazon.nova-lite-v1:0'); TABLE_NAME, SNS_TOPIC_ARN from env. VISION_PROMPT exactly as in plan.md (strict pixel-only, y increases downward, return only one JSON object with reference_object/reference_top_px/reference_bottom_px/waterline_px, nulls if unseen, NEVER output depth or metres).

Define SAMPLE_REPORTS: 2-3 dicts (one per settlement) each with settlement, timestamp (recent ISO-8601 UTC), depth_m, category_key, final_label, advice, lat, lon, reference_object. Give them differing categories so markers show color (e.g. Mathare 'dangerous', Mukuru 'impassable_boda').

Implement vision(image_bytes, fmt, reference_object): call boto3 bedrock-runtime.converse per the plan's invoke shape (image content block + text prompt, inferenceConfig maxTokens 300 temperature 0.0), extract resp['output']['message']['content'][0]['text'], parse the first {...} JSON block, return (reference_top_px, reference_bottom_px, waterline_px). Raise a clear ValueError if a value is null/unparseable so the caller returns 422 with the raw text in the trace. Never fabricate numbers.

Implement rainfall(lat, lon): urllib.request.urlopen the Open-Meteo URL from plan.md with timeout=5, sum json['hourly']['precipitation']; on any exception return 0.0 and signal that so a trace note is added.

Implement route POST /analyze: parse body JSON {settlement, reference_object, image_base64?, demo?}. Validate settlement in SETTLEMENTS and reference_object in REFERENCE_HEIGHTS_M (else 400). If demo true or no image_base64: use canned pixel coords (e.g. doorframe top=100,bottom=600,waterline=365) instead of calling Bedrock. Else base64-decode image, detect png vs jpeg, call vision(). Build DepthInput, call compute_depth; if not ok return 400 with result.error. Call rainfall(), then fuse_rainfall(result, rainfall_mm). Write a DynamoDB item (schema in plan.md; store floats as Decimal/str). Best-effort SNS publish of final_label+advice wrapped in try/except (log, never fail). Return 200 JSON with ok, settlement, depth_m, reference_object, category_key, final_label, advice, escalated, rainfall_mm, lat, lon, timestamp, and trace = result.trace + risk.trace.
Implement GET /reports: scan the table (limit ~50), sort newest first, return {reports:[...]}; if empty, return SAMPLE_REPORTS so the map is never empty. Use json.dumps(..., default=str) for Decimal.
Implement POST /seed: put each SAMPLE_REPORTS item into the table; return {seeded:n}.

Implement GET /health -> {ok:true}. Handle OPTIONS -> 204. Add CORS header Access-Control-Allow-Origin:* to every response via a shared _resp(status, body) helper. Route using event['requestContext']['http']['method'] and event['rawPath'].
Guard all boto3 clients so the module imports without AWS creds (lazy client creation inside functions) to allow a local import smoke test.
acceptance_criteria: lambda/handler.py imports cleanly when depth_engine.py is beside it (python3 -c 'import handler' from a dir containing both, with boto3 available or clients created lazily).
handler.py imports the engine symbols by the exact names REFERENCE_HEIGHTS_M, DepthInput, compute_depth, fuse_rainfall and never computes a depth itself.
The vision function parses only pixel coordinates and raises instead of inventing numbers on bad model output.
A simulated demo /analyze event (no image) returns a 200-shaped dict containing depth_m and a non-empty trace list.
GET /reports with an empty table yields the SAMPLE_REPORTS payload.
verification: python3 engine/depth_engine.py  (confirms the reused engine still passes self-check)
cp engine/depth_engine.py lambda/depth_engine.py && cd lambda && python3 -c "import handler; print('import ok')"  (lazy clients let this pass without creds)

cd lambda && python3 -c "import json,handler; e={'rawPath':'/analyze','requestContext':{'http':{'method':'POST'}},'body':json.dumps({'demo':True,'settlement':'Mathare','reference_object':'doorframe'})}; print(handler.handler(e,None))"  — expect a 200 body with depth_m and trace (DynamoDB/SNS calls may be stubbed or wrapped; demo path must still return the computed trace even if persistence is skipped locally)
findings: DONE. lambda/handler.py created; lambda/depth_engine.py is a vendored copy (produced by `cp engine/depth_engine.py lambda/depth_engine.py`) — later deploy must re-vendor before cdk synth. IMPORT STYLE (exact): `from depth_engine import REFERENCE_HEIGHTS_M, DepthInput, compute_depth, fuse_rainfall` (sibling module, NOT ../engine). Handler never computes a depth; engine does all metres. ROUTING: event['requestContext']['http']['method'] + event['rawPath']; routes POST /analyze, GET /reports, POST /seed, GET /health, OPTIONS->204, else 404. Open CORS via shared _resp(status, body) on every reply. Lazy boto3 clients (_bedrock/_table/_sns) so module imports without creds. ENV read: MODEL_ID (default amazon.nova-lite-v1:0), TABLE_NAME (default 'reports'), SNS_TOPIC_ARN (default '' -> publish skipped). DEMO COORDS (canned, used when demo:true OR no image_base64): reference_top_px=100.0, reference_bottom_px=600.0, waterline_px=365.0 -> doorframe demo = 0.95 m, category 'evacuate'. Image format detection: PNG magic header -> 'png' else 'jpeg'. vision() parses first {...} JSON block from resp['output']['message']['content'][0]['text']; raises ValueError (never fabricates) on missing/null/non-numeric -> caller returns 422 with raw text in trace. rainfall() returns (mm, ok); ok=False -> trace note, defaults 0.0, never raises. DynamoDB floats stored as Decimal via json round-trip (json.loads(json.dumps(item), parse_float=Decimal)); reads use json.dumps(default=str). SAMPLE_REPORTS: Mathare depth 0.72 'dangerous'; Mukuru depth 0.38 'impassable_boda' (distinct marker colours), timestamps = recent UTC ISO at import time. SNS publish best-effort (try/except, logs). DynamoDB write failure in /analyze is also wrapped so the deterministic trace still returns 200 (local invoke proved this). VERIFICATION (all pass): (1) `python3 engine/depth_engine.py` self-check OK. (2) vendored import `python3 -c 'import handler'` from lambda/ -> 'import ok'. (3) demo /analyze invoke -> STATUS 200, depth_m 0.95, trace_len 10, final_label 'Evacuate' (DynamoDB write failed gracefully locally, result still returned). Extra checks: /reports empty-table -> SAMPLE_REPORTS (200, 2 items); /health 200; OPTIONS 204; bad settlement 400; CORS '*'; vision() raises on null waterline and parses valid pixel JSON (120.0,580.0,400.0). Lambda needs only boto3 (runtime-provided) + stdlib (base64/json/os/re/urllib/datetime/decimal) — no pip deps, no Docker bundling. Committed locally (git init'd in kinga-maji root; no remote; NEVER pushed).
